1.1: 1.1 John, the apostle and evangelist, chosen and beloved by Christ, was held in such great love of affection that at the supper he reclined upon His breast, and that to him alone, as he stood by the cross, He commended His own mother, so that the one whom He had drawn to the embrace of virginity when he wished to marry, He also handed over to guard the Virgin. When, therefore, on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, he was allotted exile on the island of Patmos, there the Apocalypse was shown beforehand to him by the same Lord and is described, so that just as at the beginning of the canon, that is, the book of Genesis, an incorruptible beginning is foretold, so too an incorruptible end would be rendered through a virgin in the Apocalypse, saying: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. This is John, who, knowing that the day of his departure from the body had come upon him, called together his disciples at Ephesus, went down into the excavated place of his burial, and when prayer was completed gave up his spirit, being known to have been as much a stranger to the pain of death as he was free of the corruption of the flesh. Yet the arrangement of this Scripture, or the ordering of the book, is therefore not expounded by us point by point, so that a desire to inquire may be set before those who do not know, and the fruit of labor for those who seek, and the teaching of mastery be reserved for God. Argument. The Apocalypse of John begins; it has as many mysteries as words. I have said too little, and all praise is beneath the merit of the volume. In single words lie manifold understandings. The Apocalypse of Jesus Christ. He prepares the hearers and makes them well-disposed and attentive, as also there: John to the seven churches which are in Asia. Which He gave. According to His humanity Christ receives it from the Father and from the Word hypostatically united to Himself, and from the Holy Spirit. Which must come to pass. As if to say: It is inevitable that they come to pass, and it is useful that they come to pass. It is necessary that the servants suffer tribulations soon. Soon. He says soon, that they may prepare themselves, so that it may not be grievous to suffer. The labors are soon to be finished, and the rewards to be given. Brief is the labor, hastened the glory.
1.2: 1.2 Who has borne witness. Who bears witness that the words of Christ Himself are true, both those spoken concerning the Word, that is, the Divinity, and concerning the humanity of Jesus Christ. To the word of God. The Son is called the Word of God, because through Him the Father was made manifest in the world. In those things which he saw. In those things which he saw bodily, as suffering and dead; and by the mind alone, as having been with the Father before all things.
1.3: 1.3 Blessed. Christ gave these things to me, and I am blessed because I have received them. Blessed, because this is the Apocalypse of Jesus Christ, etc. He who reads. That is, he relates to others what he has heard, since many can hear from one who reads; or, they shall hear, and in this he marks the hearers, because they are many. Only those are blessed who hear in order to store it in the mind; and they store it in the mind in order to fulfill it in deed; and they fulfill it in deed in order to possess eternal life. Keeps them. For it is not the hearers of the law but the doers who are just. He keeps them who does not violate the faith of Christ and of the Church, and fears what is threatened, and seeks what is promised. Truly blessed is this man, since the labor does not last long, and the rewards are near.
1.4: 1.4 To the seven churches. He writes principally to those churches of Asia, of which he had been appointed teacher, and by likeness to the others. God gave it to Christ, Christ to John, and John to the churches, or through the seven, to the whole Church. For seven signifies totality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit. In Asia. Asia means elevation; the Church, therefore, is now in the elevation of virtues, or was formerly in that of vices. This Asia is not that great third part of the world, but a certain province where there were seven cities, and seven churches with seven bishops. Grace to you. In the greeting he prepares the hearers, and makes them well-disposed and attentive, as also in the prologue. Who is and who was. Eternally. Although He was born in time, He who was once corruptible is now unchangeable through His humanity. Such will He come, even if He does not appear such to the world. And from the seven spirits who are before. Spirit. This has the same sound as charity. Hence the remission of sins is attributed to the Spirit, and other gifts which are the gifts of the whole Trinity, so that we may understand that the Trinity works from love alone. He is silent about the person of the Father, because no one had understood anything evil about God the Creator; he sets down the person of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, about whom all the heresies in the churches are born. Throne. The thrones of God are His angels and holy men, in whom God now sits and judges, so that He may not have to judge in the future.
1.5: 1.5 The faithful witness. He says this on account of those despairing over the death of Christ, like those who said: We hoped that He was the one to redeem Israel (Luke 24). The firstborn of the dead. As if to say: Let it not terrify you, for He has risen and is impassible. Or He is the first of those who mortify themselves, because He committed no sin. The prince of the kings of the earth. The prince of earthly powers, able to remove them, and for the benefit of His own or of the saints allowing the wicked to serve.
1.6: 1.6 And He has made us a kingdom for our God. That is, able to resist vices; and priests, that is, offering ourselves to God for ourselves and for our brethren.
1.7: 1.7 Behold, He comes, etc. And truly you ought to glorify Him, because He is the one who is to come to repay. With the clouds, that is, with the saints: for they were clouds by raining down teaching on others and by working miracles; or, as He ascended in a cloud, so He will come in a cloud, by which we understand God's mercy, in which there is refreshment and illumination for the good, but terror and blinding for the wicked. This too was signified by the cloud by which the children of Israel were led out of Egypt. And He will see Him. Another translation has: All the earth will see such a one. As if to say: They will see Him as such as the wicked did not believe He would come. Every eye. The good will see Him that they may rejoice, the wicked that they may be confounded. They will lament. Or they will dash against Him, unable to resist His authority, like a stone against earthenware. Or they will beat themselves, that is, they will grieve, looking at those who are founded upon Him, because they will grieve not so much over the torment itself as that they will be cast out from such fellowship.
1.8: 1.8 I am. Truly He will come, because He Himself promises that He will come. Or, having put forward the greeting, he makes them attentive, as if to say: Believe that this was not said by me, but by Christ Himself. Alpha, the beginning. Before whom there was no one, or from whom all things began. Omega, the end. After whom there is no one, or in whom all things will be completed.
1.9: 1.9 I, John. The greeting finished, he proceeds to the narration, setting down four things: the person, the place, the cause of the place, and the time, which serve to commend the revelation itself. I, John. As if to say: I know that you are in tribulation, but may you suffer patiently by the example of Christ, that you may be partakers of His kingdom. Your brother, etc., in Christ. In the unity of faith, and on account of that faith I was in tribulation, as others were, through which I patiently endured to arrive at the kingdom, having Christ as an example in all things. Patmos. That is, a strait, namely tribulation, in which heavenly things are more opened to the faithful. The Church is compared to an island, because as an island is battered by sea storms, so the Church is afflicted by the persecutions of the marine, that is, the worldly. For the word of God. That is, for the testimony rendered to the divinity and humanity.
1.10: 1.10 On the Lord's day. The quality of things is usually marked by the time: thus Abraham saw the angel at midday in the fervor of faith; Lot at evening, at the destruction of Sodom; Adam heard the voice of the Lord after midday; Solomon, who was not going to keep it, received wisdom by night. I heard behind me a voice. He heard behind himself, because while, led out from present things, he stretched himself toward the forward things of true contemplation, he was also admonished to look back at others; or: he hears behind himself, because this was foretold by the law and the prophets, for that is what he understands.
1.11: 1.11 What you see, write. A common admonition is given to John, who admonished that it be sent in common to the churches of Asia, through which all the other Churches are to be understood. This common admonition is made down to: And to the angel of Ephesus, etc. Whether John saw this vision all at once and in a single glance, or at different times, the angel could have conferred it on him either way. At Ephesus. Ephesus is interpreted as my will, or a deep fall, or counsel.
1.12: 1.12 And I turned. And because I heard the voice, I turned, etc. Seven lampstands. That is, seven churches burning and illuminated by the wisdom of the divine Word. Golden. As gold, proved by fire and stretched by blows, is made into a lampstand, so the Church, purified by tribulations and extended into long-suffering by the strokes of temptations, is brought to perfection; and if she has a voice in the mouth and not in deed, she is indeed a lampstand, but not a golden one.
1.13: 1.13 Like the Son of man. That is, an angel in the person of Christ, who is no longer called Son of man, but like, because He no longer dies. Or like the Son of man, because Christ appeared not with sin but in the likeness of sinful flesh, in whom are all things necessary for the governing of the Church. In a long robe. That is, in a priestly garment, that is, the flesh in which He offered Himself, and daily offers, presenting Himself to God the Father. Or, the long robe is the Church, with which God is clothed as with a tunic, which is called ankle-length, because the Church will last until the end of the world. Girded about the breasts. Daniel saw one girded about the loins in the Old Testament, because there carnal things are restrained; here we read of one girded about the breasts, because in the New Testament even thoughts are judged.
1.14: 1.14 His hairs were white. That is, the saints, made fine and clinging to the head itself. Or His thoughts. Like wool. As white wool is apt to receive any colors whatever, so the saints are apt to endure tribulations. Snow. Snow is the whiteness of immortality, because it is whiter than every creature. Eyes. That is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit: these are Christ's as of one having and giving them, just as the Church's as of one receiving them; these illuminate and make burn. Or the eyes are the spiritual men themselves in the Church, or the divine precepts.
1.15: 1.15 And His feet. That is, the last of the faithful, who, through many shakings, will not retain their former nature, like fine brass, which is often set on fire and takes on a better color. In a burning furnace. In another translation it is: like the brass of Lebanon, by which it is shown that in that region where the Lord was crucified that tribulation will chiefly prevail. And His voice as the voice of many waters. That is, His preaching has the force of water, because it cleanses. Or because many peoples (who are compared to water on account of flowing) have now received this voice, you ought to stand firm all the more. Or a voice that gives many waters, that is, graces; hence there follows at once:
1.16: 1.16 Stars. The stars are bishops, who ought to shine for others by word and by the example of life; even if they sin, they are called stars, according to how they were appointed: these He holds in His right hand, that is, in the greater gifts, which are signified by the right hand. And out of His mouth. That is, by God's inspiration there came forth preaching, which cuts both ways: in the Old Testament, carnal works, but in the New, concupiscences; hence of this sword, which is the word of God, it is written: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you. As the sun shines in its power. That is, at midday without clouds. Or, as Christ Himself in the resurrection; or, when He shall be fixed forever.
1.17: 1.17 I fell. That is, I cast aside concern for humanity, in likeness to the last of the faithful. As dead. Dead to the world, alive to God, and desiring nothing earthly. His right hand. Namely the Holy Spirit comforting, that is, His help. Do not be afraid. To suffer tribulations and death for me, because I, who did not need it for my own sake, since I am the first and the last, was dead and am alive.
1.18: 1.18 I am living. And therefore do not be terrified, because I have manifestly risen and shall die no more. And I have. And therefore I will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, because I have power over the devil and over his members. Of death and of hell. The devil is death, because he is the cause of sin, that is, of death; his ministers are hell, in whom he has a place.
1.19: 1.19 What must come to pass after these things. In the last of the faithful, by whose example these ought to be greatly encouraged.
1.20: 1.20 The mystery. Namely the sacred secret, where one thing is seen and another understood. This first vision concerns the rebuke of the churches. The angel opens the allegory in part, to teach that it ought to be sought everywhere.
2.1: 2.1 And to the angel. That is, he writes to the bishop, from whose hand He requires the sins of his subjects, and without whose consent John himself does not presume to judge the subjects. Of the church of Ephesus. Ephesus, in respect of the part of those who persevere well, is interpreted as will, those in whose works God delights, of whom He sets forth that by their example those who had fallen may be corrected. Likewise Ephesus is interpreted as counsel, that is, in need of counsel, or a deep fall, or my will. Seven. He begins the individual admonitions, which, though individual, can also be universal according to the different members of any church. You cannot bear. By the force of humanity. Or, you cannot bear without amending or expelling.
2.2: 2.2 You have tried those who call themselves. None are tried except those who are within the Church.
2.3: 2.3 You have borne for My name. You did not do this for human praise, but for the glorifying of My name. And you have not failed. He notes that the cause of human failing would have been present had help not come first.
2.4: 2.4 But I have against you that charity. Either the bishop in his own person, affected by weariness of vices, is rebuked in his subjects, or the subjects are found to offend through love of earthly things. Eli the priest was good, and yet he was condemned because he would not correct his sons.
2.5: 2.5 I will move the lampstand. I will take away the virtues and gifts of the Holy Spirit, through which the lampstands are established.
2.6: 2.6 But this you have that is good. Although this is against you, yet do not despair, because you have something good. The works of the Nicolaites. That is, the common use of women, and the eating of things sacrificed to idols.
2.7: 2.7 He who has an ear. Why must it be heard? Because to him who perseveres Christ is the tree of life, since He is shade and strength and the giver of fruit, that is, His body and blood, both here and above all in the future.
2.8: 2.8 Of Smyrna. Smyrna is interpreted as song, or as it were myrrh: a song in those in whom He delights; myrrh is so bitter that it even preserves bodies from decay. These things says the First. He describes Christ in such a way as to avail for the consolation of those on whom tribulations are laid. These things says the First. As if to say: Do not fail, because I, so great, suffered death for your sake, and rose from it. Expect the same also for yourselves.
2.10: 2.10 Some of you. Here it is clear that it is understood not of one only, but of several. That you may be tried. That is, that you may be proved, or may be held in contempt by the devil and his members. Ten days. That is, the time of that war. For God, sending His own to war, arms them with the Decalogue. Or ten days, that is, this whole time in which, through seven days, the fight is against three principal vices: avarice, cupidity, and vainglory.
2.11: 2.11 By the second death. The first death of the soul is in sins, the second in punishments; the first death of the body is when it is dissolved, the second when it shall be condemned in judgment.
2.12: 2.12 The sword. He requires that these have this sword in the choosing of the good and the rejecting of the wicked.
2.13: 2.13 You have not denied My faith. Tribulation is illumination for the just, correction for the stubborn, blinding for the obstinate.
2.14: 2.14 Balaam. By Balaam are to be understood the heretics who teach earthly princes how they may overthrow the worshippers of the true God. Or Balaam, that is, the demons, who teach the flesh to deceive souls that see God.
2.15: 2.15 The doctrine of the Nicolaites. He repeats about the Nicolaites in order to invite to repentance, which they had not done.
2.17: 2.17 Manna. By manna understand eternal glory, of which all will say: What is this? For neither has eye seen, nor ear heard (1 Cor. 2), etc. And I will give him. In Daniel it is written: A stone was cut out without hands (Dan. 1). In Proverbs: The expectation of one who waits is a most weighty gem (Prov. 17). The same, a solid body, bright through itself, white with virtues and the hope of immortality. And in a stone. Or add martyrdom above baptism, the force of which the hypocrite, who suffers for the praise of men, does not understand. Written. With five letters, namely the five wounds with which His body was shown on the cross, because He was a martyr.
2.19: 2.19 I know your works, etc. The Son has the gifts of the Holy Spirit, that is, gives to whom he will, or takes away. Therefore let those see who have already received those gifts, lest by consent to the wicked they lose them. Or understand charity and faith, so that the order be backward; for charity is not before faith. First faith, from faith charity, from charity good works.
2.20: 2.20 To commit fornication. Fornication is said to be fourfold in the mind, If you see a woman to lust after her, Matthew 5., etc. In the act itself, in the love of earthly things, in the worship of idols.
2.24: 2.24 I will not send. Some false teachers terrified them by saying that the Lord would yet send greater tribulations than they had suffered: against this he says that he will not send.
3.1: 3.1 And to the angel of the Church of Sardis. Sardis is interpreted beginning of beauty, and by this is signified one who at first has no or little virtue, then becomes foul through vices; or hypocrites are understood who are beautiful outside, deformed within. I know your works. And I know that in all your works you seek human praise.
3.2: 3.2 Be watchful. Therefore watch, because though you be unmoved in mind, or praiseworthy in mind, you are not perfect unless you rouse the rest, and it is not enough to confess Christ unless you also have done works. For I find not your works full. While you are without charity, either for praise, or because you commit a capital crime.
3.3: 3.3 Have in mind therefore. That is, remember how you received the faith of Christ in baptism: where you promised to renounce the devil and all his pomps. Remember also that you have heard from the teachers of the Christian faith how you ought to live: and keep what you heard, and do penance, because you have been so long torpid from good works. You have heard from the holy Fathers that he who offends in one point is guilty of all; whence, And have not charity, I am nothing, James 2.
3.4: 3.4 Have not defiled their garments. The garments of immortality and innocence which they received in baptism, or, their good works.
3.5: 3.5 I will not blot out. He blots out the reprobate, according to that: The Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, Exodus 10. Out of the book of life. The book of life is the foreknowledge of God, in which all things are contained. I will confess his name, saying: Come, blessed of my Father, Matthew 25. Or here, You gave me to eat and to drink.
3.7: 3.7 These things says. As if he said: Labor for the conversion of the brethren as you have begun: because in what I promised, whatsoever you shall ask the Father in my name, he will give you, John 14., I am true in promises, whence you may know that I will gather many for you as you desire. Shuts. That we may seek, opens, that we may find, that the inquirer may receive the fruit of his sweat, and the giver have thanks for the grace of his goodness.
3.8: 3.8 Behold I have given before you. Deservedly I have given, because openly you could not have through yourself, because you have little strength. A door. By the door, called ostium from obstare, are understood the hearts of men hard before. Or you can understand obscure Scriptures. Or Christ, who is the true door to life, whence the disciples forbidden to speak and beaten said: We cannot but speak the things we have seen, Acts 4.
3.9: 3.9 The Jews. This name they lost when they said of Christ: This man we know not, John 9. They lie. They strive to prove by words and certain pretenses. Behold I will make them come. Ready to imitate your works through likeness to your humility. They shall know. Those placed outside did not believe God loved the Church which he permitted to be afflicted, but now he will make the faith of love, that is certainty, lest you succumb, because I come to reward.
3.10: 3.10 You have kept the word of my patience. The precept of patience which I showed in myself, praying for persecutors. From the hour of temptation, either of the general persecution of Christians to come immediately after Nero, or of the last time of Antichrist. To try them that dwell upon the earth. As in the following, more often in the sixth order, so also here in the sixth angel the last persecution is designated, in which some of the Jews are to be deceived: some, by the admonitions of Elijah, about to fulfill the law spiritually, believe they will conquer the enemy.
3.11: 3.11 Behold I come quickly. As if he said: The temptation will indeed come, but succumb not, because I come to reward.
3.12: 3.12 A pillar in the temple. Firm in himself and sustaining others by word and example. He shall go out no more. Since God has a fixed number of his own, if any slips, another is brought in by his mercy, as through the pride of the Jews the Gentiles came in. The younger son, that is the people of the Gentiles, had gone out, but by the death of the fatted calf, that is the blood of Christ, reconciled, will go out no more. New. Where nothing of oldness, but the full vision of peace. Out of heaven. From the conformity of heavenly creatures.
3.14: 3.14 The witness, of what he heard from the Father, fearless. Or, to whom faith is to be given in all things. Or, witness of our works before the Father. And true. He is truth, because through him the promises of the Father are fulfilled.
3.15: 3.15 You are neither cold nor hot, because you neither wholly ignore the faith, nor openly deny it once received. Would you were cold. He does not wish him cold simply, but such a one of whom greater hope may be had.
3.16: 3.16 I will begin to vomit you out. About to say a wonderful thing, that the lukewarm were to be excommunicated, because they were believed good by men, he says he is truthful in all things, that in this he be believed, and if they will repent, he promises preservation, because he gave the first faith. Out of my mouth. He is vomited from the mouth who is cast down into worse things or who dies impenitent.
3.17: 3.17 I am rich, in divine knowledge, or secular.
3.18: 3.18 I counsel you to buy of me gold fire-tried. Because such works will not lead to salvation. That the shame of your nakedness appear not. It is better here to blush before a few than in the future before all. Eye-salve. The eyes, that we may see, are anointed, when to know the brightness of the true light we help the keenness of our understanding with the medicine of good working. The commandment of the Lord enlightening the eyes, Psalm 18. Or anoint with the gift of the Holy Spirit the mind which earthly things had shut up.
3.20: 3.20 Behold I stand at the door and knock. If any man shall hear, etc. I wait, or inspire, or call by preachers.
3.21: 3.21 To sit with me on my throne. To judge in those in whom I sit and judge. This of prelates, and, through prelates, of subjects. As I also have overcome and am set down with my Father in his throne. This he says so, because the victory and session of Christ is the cause of the victory and session of Christians.
4.1: 4.1 After these things I saw. In this second vision he treats of him that sits on the throne, and of his adornment, and of the lamb opening the book, that is the divine disposition for the repair of the human race, and of him loosing the seven seals, that is the obscurities, that when we have seen that God has bestowed on men so great an understanding of the Scriptures, we may be grateful to him, and not fear to suffer for him. In heaven. That is in Scripture, which is the way to life, or Christ is the door, whose mysteries, before closed, are now opened to those who by faith and work are heaven. As of a trumpet speaking with me. Not disagreeing with my rationality, by giving these reasons. I will show you. The things having been said which are already past, he also says those that must yet be done, as about to remain in the same state in which they began. Or, after correction it is needful to see the secrets by which they are animated for the battles. Or, the things that must shortly be done after these, that is in the last faithful. Or, after these things I was in the spirit.
4.2: 4.2 Immediately I was. I did not resist, but cast away the care of all earthliness. And behold a throne. In which God sits and judges, and also the subjects of whom some are so fit that God fittingly sits and rests in them. Sitting. Christ above was said to walk among the candlesticks, now sitting, that is judging the merits of each, of whom he fittingly makes memory here, whom he exhorted to the fight.
4.3: 4.3 He that sat. Where there are only good, there is no need to judge, that is to discern; where good and bad, there discernment is needed. Was like in appearance. Before, unknown, he appeared to the world through the flesh, breaking his enemies, giving strength to his own. Of jasper and sardine. By the color of two stones he marks God and man. Emerald. By the green color of the emerald, which is a watery color, baptism is understood. By its redness, the gifts of the Holy Spirit received in baptism, by which sins are burned away.
4.4: 4.4 Twenty-four ancients. Twelve prophets, twelve apostles, though more of each order. Clothed in white garments. The sins of the just are covered, and they themselves grow white with virtues. Crowns. That is victory through wisdom and charity even toward enemies.
4.5: 4.5 From the throne. That is the Church, that is water rains lightnings, that is miracles which terrify and illuminate. Seven spirits. The lamps are the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which kindle and illuminate, ready for all those who are the seats of God.
4.6: 4.6 In the sight. Because they understand the sacrament and the thing of the sacrament, nor receive any but those whom they have seen and known to be fit. A sea of glass. Baptism bright with sincerity of faith, after which, through the fire of tribulation, the elect are led to firmness of good works, as crystal hardens from water. In the midst. He describes a certain plain that appeared, in the likeness of a great judge, who has a broad and spacious street where he sits and judges judgments. Of the seat. By the name of seat is understood Jerusalem, or supporters, as a man, as a calf, as a lion, as an eagle. Four. On account of the office of fourfold preaching. Living creatures. These well represent Christ, who was born, suffered, rose, ascended. The faithful also are rational and meek, like the man. Fearlessly treading down adversities, like the lion; mortifying themselves, like the calf; seeking heavenly things, like the eagle. Full of eyes. Mindful of past sins, and guarding themselves for the future, or having knowledge of what God has done or will do at the end of the world, or pleasing God and men.
4.7: 4.7 The lion. The lion is born dead, on the third day is quickened by the voice of the Father. So also Christ rose on the third day, and it behooved him to rise, because he was dead, and it behooved him to die, because man, and being dead he willed and was able to rise, because eagle, that is God.
4.8: 4.8 And the four living creatures had each of them six wings, to the end that they preach these things of Christ in which they were well instructed. Six wings. The first wing, the natural law; the second, the law of Moses; the third, the prophets; the fourth, the Gospel; the fifth, the institutions of the apostles; the sixth, the decrees of whomever, as of Augustine, Gregory, Ambrose, by whom the Church seeks the heights: and from whom preachers receive the foundation of all preaching. Or the six wings are the knowledge of the works of God done in six days, the knowledge of which they lift on high who work well in them. Round about and within. By the letter, the simple; by allegory, the more perfect, these living creatures instruct, and enlighten in the midst and in the ends of the earth. They are full of eyes. Because they keep themselves clean and form others by example. Or, they are full of eyes within, that is a clean conscience: and round about, that is in the sight of men irreproachable. Who is to come. The Son will appear bodily, the whole Godhead will manifest itself to the faithful in its own manner.
4.9: 4.9 And benediction, of the heavenly reward, or in exaltation, that to him every knee may bow of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth, Philippians 2.
4.10: 4.10 And they adored. What they had not from themselves they sought from him in voice and work. Saying. In the secret of the heart ascribing to God the victory over vices and tribulations.
4.11: 4.11 You have created all things. Therefore all things are to be referred to you, because all things have their beginning from you. The invisible also, either angels or souls, as he says they are spiritual, when from the wicked he makes the pious spiritually created. For your will. And not suddenly. And what was made, in him was life, John 1. They were. In mind, before they were formed in work. They were created. By existing visibly. All things therefore were from eternity according as they were in the divine mind, but began to be in time by creation.
5.1: 5.1 And I saw in the right hand of him that sat. By the right hand I understand the Son, through whom God the Father made all things, to whom the intention of the whole book is directed. A book. That is the two Testaments, which are the same book. Written within. Signifying the Old, which promises outward things. And on the back, signifying the New, which often evidently promises beatitude. Sealed. The writings of the prophets were made closed and obscure, but through Christ afterward were opened. With seals. That is, with all obscurities, or closed by the sevenfold spirit, through whom faith is opened. Seven. He says so because (as he will determine in what follows) those are the seven seals, namely that the horse is white, and red, and black, etc.: which were opened and known at the beginning of the Church, which was the white horse on which Christ sat, and fortified by doctrine and example, which the red horse assailed.
5.2: 5.2 An angel. The holy and ancient fathers of the Old Testament understood that the restoration of Jerusalem was at some time arranged by God: and when it would be done they longed to see, but how it would be done they knew not, until it was revealed to some before it happened. Preaching. Inquiring, and announcing to others and, from excessive desire, complaining that it was so long delayed. To open the book. The divine disposition, and to take away all the obscurities of the Scriptures.
5.4: 5.4 I wept much. This is said in the person of the former and ancient fathers, because they did not understand, or grieved at the delayed restoration, whence: Many kings and prophets have desired to see, Luke 10., etc.
5.5: 5.5 And one of the ancients. Any prophet, by announcing the coming of Christ, consoles the others. The lion hath overcome. The lion when pursued flees through the mountains, and with the tuft he has on his tail wipes out his footprints, that he not be found: so Christ fled through the mountains, that is, the divinity lay hid from the Jews, the flesh assumed covered the divinity, that it could not be recognized. The lion sleeps with open eyes, so Christ expired with the divinity living.
5.6: 5.6 And behold in the midst of the throne. The Church, which is possessed by Christ as a throne, is fed as the living creatures, is honored as the ancients in the judgment of power, herself built upon Christ, in seven horns of strength is exalted with the kingdom, in seven eyes is enlightened with signs and virtues. As it were slain. Because though he was dead, yet by the power of God he lives. Or among his own he is as it were slain, in whom he is daily mortified. Seven horns, etc. Because he gives the kingdom, which is marked in horns. Eyes, because he enlightens. Or the horns are the more eminent saints, founded in Christ the head, surpassing the flesh.
5.8: 5.8 Fell down before the lamb. They thought humbly of themselves, because they imitate him, whence follows. Having every one harps. The mortifications of vices and concupiscences. In a harp are wood and strings: by the wood the cross of Christ, by the strings the flesh of the saints, which is stretched on the wood, while, giving the same sound under diverse torments, they imitate the cross of Christ.
5.9: 5.9 They sung a new canticle. With exultation the Church professes the New Testament by deed, while she baptizes in his death. Tribe. So called from three orders, in which are seventy-two tongues in each, of which many peoples, in the people nations. Three orders of those to be saved, Noah, Daniel, Job. Or three orders of nations, Greeks, Hebrews, Christians.
5.11: 5.11 I saw. Not only the living creatures and ancients attesting the same by their office, but I also heard, The voice of angels. That is, of the heavenly spirits who guard and keep the Church, who rejoice at the repaired fellowship of the saints, who bear witness to Christ, and at the nativity, when they appeared to the shepherds, and in the passion, and in the resurrection and ascension attested that the judge would come. Or the angels are the lesser subjects in the Church, leading an angelic life, who surround and honor their preachers and their judges, agreeing with their testimony and conforming themselves. Of many round about the throne, and the living creatures, and the ancients, etc. The more numerous, the greater the attestation, and the greater joy. Thousands of thousands. He set down this number, because what is infinite to men is finite with God.
5.12: 5.12 Wisdom, and strength, etc. The knowledge of all things, as the Word united to him has.
5.13: 5.13 Blessing. That is, the increase that we have in good works, and the honor that follows therefrom, and the glory of the virtues we receive in baptism, and the power by which we resist concupiscences, be ascribed not to us, but to you.
5.14: 5.14 And the four living creatures. All the ancients and living creatures give assent to the testimony of the angels. Fell on their faces, etc. They are not proud that they judge others, but humble themselves.
6.1: 6.1 And I saw. After the Lamb fulfilled what had been foretold of himself and strengthened his Church in faith by the testimony of the prophets and angels, he opened to them the sense that they may understand the Scriptures, and through preachers announces outwardly what it behooves to suffer for this faith, and what helps or what crowns he sets before his own, because, after making memory of the restoration, if he were silent about tribulations, they could already fail, if tribulation should arise unexpectedly. When he had opened. This book was sealed, because Christ opened all things either in himself or in his own. For he himself opened to his own the senses, that they might understand these seals in the Scriptures. In the first seal opened, whence went forth the white horse, is understood the whitening of the Church by baptism. In the second, the red horse, the open persecution of those shedding blood is insinuated, whence tribulations rise against the baptized. In the third, the black, the hidden persecution of heretics. In the fourth, the pale, the open and hidden persecution of false accusations. Come and see. Pass from the mystery, and see the full truth or justice.
6.2: 6.2 Behold a white horse. The Church whitened in baptism, or the greatest preachers, who carry God everywhere. A bow. Christ has the Scripture by which he enlightens his own, and slays enemies.
6.3: 6.3 And when he had opened the second seal. The devil, seeing the Church established to fill up the place whence he himself had fallen, strives to overthrow her, first openly. A red horse. Contrary to the former, namely open persecutors and bloody.
6.4: 6.4 To take peace from the earth, and that, etc. That is, it was granted by God that he take away all quiet of mind from those who are given to earthly things. And a great sword was given to him. Great power of killing, because not only against the lesser but also against the greater, as Peter, he dared to rage.
6.5: 6.5 And behold a black horse. The devil, seeing that he had not prospered by open persecutions, sends heretics, who contend with false reasons that they may deceive the more easily. A balance. Because they say they have true discernment in the Scriptures.
6.6: 6.6 And I heard as it were. Because here in the fight of heretics, where there is greater danger, help is held forth. Two pounds. As if he said: O faithful, fear not those who before could harm you; and you devils, do not harm these, because you shall not prevail, because two pounds of wheat, etc. Of wheat. By wheat are understood the more perfect, who, ground by tribulation, are baked by fire, sweet food for God. Barley are the lesser of the same kind. Wine, pressed indeed by the press, but not so baked, sharp only in themselves, and making others drunk to do well: oil are those not making others drunk, but first anointing with prayers. And hurt not the wine and oil. That is those who are refreshed with wine, that is my blood, and anointed with oil, that is the Holy Spirit. Wine likewise is bought for one penny.
6.8: 6.8 Behold a pale horse. The devil, seeing he cannot prosper either by open tribulations or open heresies, sends false brethren ahead: who under the habit of religion take on the nature of the red horse and the black, perverting the faith. His name was Death. Because through him death came in, or literally because he kills some in the flesh, some in the soul. And hell. That is the insatiable who imitate him with earthly things, and are put in hell. Over the four. That is over all the wicked dwelling everywhere, or over Jews and Gentiles, heretics and false Christians.
6.9: 6.9 And when. The tribulations shown that threaten the faithful in the present, that they fail not, he consoles the suffering by somewhat assuring them of the near crown. I saw under the altar. That is humbling themselves to their head, or, under, in hiding, because no one in this life perceives how they are there. The altar. Christ upon whom all the saints offer themselves, and whom they have as their defense. Or the souls themselves are the altar from which smoke goes up delightful to God, and because they were smeared with blood, now they are beneath, that is in a lesser dignity than they will be, because they have as yet received but one robe. Of them that were slain for the word. Either by open martyrdom, or by some anxieties.
6.10: 6.10 How long. The saints desire greater joy and the fellowship of saints, and agree to the justice of God in the damnation of the impious. Do you not judge and revenge our blood. By making the discernment of the good and the wicked.
6.11: 6.11 Their fellow servants. They are called servants for the sake of the Lord himself, as brethren they ought to wait from love.
6.12: 6.12 The sun became black. That is, those in whom he shines will be reputed guilty and sinners, holding back their own brightness, or because some will fall into darkness. Or Christ the true sun, now bright, in the time of Antichrist will be obscure, that is shining with no miracles. As sackcloth. Light placed in a sack shines not outside; the faithful will not pour forth the light of preaching on that day of great tribulation.
6.13: 6.13 Her green figs. That is empty fruits, for God permits none to fall who serves him with true love.
6.14: 6.14 Heaven. That is the Church will withdraw from evils, in faith and work. Whence: Go out of Babylon, my people, and touch not the unclean thing.
6.15: 6.15 The kings of the earth. According to the various honors of the world which, unwilling to lose, they destroy the faith. The rich. Fulfilling whatever evils they will. The mighty. In overthrowing others. The servant of sin, free from justice. These despairing of the saints seek the helps of demons, to free themselves from those in whom they trusted.
6.16: 6.16 And they say to the mountains. Let them seek the suffrages of the angels, who are the more eminent mountains, and rocks by firmness: that by their prayers they may obtain the mercy of the judge.
7.1: 7.1 After these things, etc. The manifold war of the Church having been described, he adds that in the time of this war the devil is ready to harm, but restrained by God, that his own may not in any way grow torpid or despair. Four angels. For the four parts of the world in which they harm. Angels. The devil is called an angel, that is sent by God for the trial of the good, and permitted for the deception of the wicked and sent by the prince, the devil, for the overthrow of all. Holding. In the time of tribulation nothing is more necessary than preaching, and therefore the devil strives to hold it back in every place. The winds. The wind stirs the clouds, watering the earth makes it fruitful, makes its face cheerful, so preaching the minds of men. On the sea. On those dwelling in islands or abounding in various vices.
7.2: 7.2 And I saw another. This angel is that stone cut out without hands, which broke the statue made of four metals, this looses the four winds. Ascending. From when Christ expired he ascends, while he bound the devil, and through preachers illumined the world with faith, as the sun with light. Or he ascends from the rising, that is from the Father, advancing in wisdom and age. Or he descends from himself, because not through intercourse of man did he take flesh, but he himself created it who is the rising of the sun, that is of the Father. The sign. That is the cross with which he signed his own, or power equal to the Father, or immunity from sin by which God appears, because every man is a sinner. This sign the ancient fathers bore, if not in fact, yet in faith. The sign is borne on the forehead that it be not hidden in tribulation, for the signing of the breast is the confession of the heart. When an infant is catechized, he is anointed on the breast, that he may have the faith of the heart: on the forehead lest he be ashamed, but confess: For with the heart we believe unto justice, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation, Romans 10. On the shoulders, that he may bear the burden of Christ. On the crown, that he may preserve reason, which is the crown and head of the inner man.
7.4: 7.4 A hundred forty-four. He puts a finite number, because God embraces all under a fixed number for himself. Of every tribe. That is of all who imitate the faith of Jacob.
7.5: 7.5 Twelve. By twelve we have those who by faith in the Trinity have been signed in the four parts of the world, and that we may show these perfect, we multiply twelve by four, and they become forty-eight; but that this perfection may be referred to the Trinity, we multiply forty-eight, and so they become a hundred sixty-four.
7.7: 7.7 Simeon. The hearing of sadness or sorrow, that is, grieving over past sins and aspiring to the conversation of virtue. Levi. That is added, that is doing even what is not enjoined on him. Issachar. That is reward, that is tending to remuneration, as: I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ.
7.8: 7.8 Zabulon. That is dwelling of strength, that is not refusing labor, but sometimes for the need of the brethren descending from Mary to Martha. Joseph. That is increase, that is enriching the Church with the number of the saints. Benjamin. That is son of the right hand, that is reckoning all things from the propitiation of God, and nothing from themselves.
7.9: 7.9 After these things. When according to the figure he had seen them designated under a fixed number, and only of the children of Israel, now he openly teaches that by that number all the faithful are to be understood, and by the twelve tribes all nations. Standing. Ready, namely, to obey God the judge, or also their prelates. This in the present.
7.10: 7.10 Salvation to our God who sits. Not through ourselves, but through the lamb we have salvation, that is remission of sins, and good working, and eternal glory.
7.11: 7.11 And all. By the angels mentioned above can be understood the greater prelates; by these, the lesser prelates, or subjects only, as are angels and archangels, and yet all angels, that is messengers. But even now there are greater and lesser prelates, that is archbishops and bishops.
7.12: 7.12 Amen. As if to say: If you ascribe to God, you do well. Or amen is to be read with what follows: Amen, that is truth in what is premised, and blessing, that is the exaltation he has above all creation, or our exaltation in virtues: and brightness, that is impassibility, or yours in works.
7.13: 7.13 And one answered. The crowd seen in so great dignity, he is moved to attend by what way they could ascend thither, that he may teach others to look likewise.
7.14: 7.14 Their robes, etc. The innocence received in baptism, or their bodies.
7.16: 7.16 They shall no more hunger, nor thirst, etc. He who gave knowledge to the angels will give the same knowledge to them also.
7.17: 7.17 Shall lead them to the fountains of life, etc. And thereby in the future will lead to all manner of refreshment. God shall wipe away every tear. Every sorrow either for their sins, or for adversities, or exile, or the rest of this kind.
8.1: 8.1 And when he had opened. In this third vision of life are seven angels sounding trumpets for the destruction of enemies, like those who by sounding trumpets destroyed the walls of Jericho. As if to say: When I had understood the salvation of the just, on the other side I understood the damnation of the impious through the office of preaching enjoined on the good.
8.2: 8.2 Seven angels. All, or imbued with the sevenfold Spirit. And there were given. Because the damnation of the impious does not displease God.
8.3: 8.3 And another angel. The angel stood before the altar ready to sacrifice, like a priest, or Christ is the altar who offered himself, and upon whom the Church offers prayers to God. He stood before the altar, that is before himself, because he has no mediator through whom to please. Having. About to say that damnation of the impious will come from the preaching of the just, he puts first as it were an excuse, lest the blame for the damnation of the impious be imputed to them, because as far as they are concerned their preaching is good, and enjoined by a good teacher. A censer. That is the apostles, who are vessels of fire, that is of the Holy Spirit, and from whom come the prayers which are lifted up before God. Of the prayers. He said of the prayers, and not the prayers, because he does not present all prayers to the Father, but hears those that pertain to salvation. Of the prayers, because they sometimes ask what ought not to be asked, as Paul. Upon the golden altar. That is, him who is above himself according to humanity, according to which he is the altar of the Trinity.
8.4: 8.4 Smoke. Compunction produced by zeal in prayer, inwardly kindled by the fire of the vision of God.
8.6: 8.6 Prepared themselves. That is, first fulfilled in work what they were to say with the mouth. Or, prepared themselves, that is foresaw what suited each person. And the first angel. In the order of narration, or because this blindness of the Jews first happened to the preaching apostles.
8.7: 8.7 And there was hail. That is preaching sweet to others seemed to them thick and heavy. Upon the earth. The Jews are like earth cultivated by the law and the prophets. Of trees. By trees are understood the greater Jews; who lived blamelessly in the law.
8.8: 8.8 And the second angel, according to the order of narration, and according to what was fulfilled. For the Jews blinded, the apostles were turned to the Gentiles. Into the sea. The Gentiles are the sea, that is flowing into many vices; in which, though the devil was before, yet he is truly said to be sent, because some departing he strives to hold others.
8.9: 8.9 The third part died. Two parts, that is all the good believed: the third, that is all the reprobate were given up to a reprobate sense. Which had souls, etc. That is of those Gentiles who were reputed more worthy by others for some good works.
8.10: 8.10 And the third angel, in the order of narration and because this happened after those two. For after the devil could not blind all the Jews and Gentiles, he sent heretics among them, and overthrew some. Fountains. Those are called fountains in which the sum and as it were the origin of the whole faith is contained, as is the Gospel. Rivers, which are drawn from there, as are the expositions of them, in which are the two senses of the faithful, historical and allegorical. The third is that of the heretics, when they confirm their heresies by perverse expositions of the Scriptures.
8.12: 8.12 And the fourth angel. Fourth is said in the order of narration, and in the order of the matter. For when the devil had blinded some of the Jews and Gentiles, at last he came out to assail the very children of the Church, and snatched some, both greater and lesser. These four damnations he related as past, as those seen daily in the churches. The three future he makes announced, to teach that in the last times even graver than the past impend, which also can be turned to the consolation of those present.
8.13: 8.13 Of one eagle. The eagle is all preachers, who with far-reaching mind gaze, and going round the Church, by foretelling the future, fortify it: here all are one, because they tend to the same.
9.1: 9.1 And the fifth angel. In order of narration and in order of time this angel is said to be the fourth. For this is the damnation of those whom the devil sends to prepare the ways before the face of Antichrist. And I saw a star. That is the flame of heretics of which he had said little, and from what tinder it grew he explains. A star. That is the devil falling, and laboring that none go into his place, that is into paradise. And there was given. The abyss, that is the dark. The pit, that is the deeper heretics, because they plunge others with perverse opinions. Into these he is said to receive the key, that is power, because then he will not be restrained by God as now. Or that key is the princes themselves through whom the heretics work.
9.2: 9.2 He opened the bottomless pit. He caused the heresies that lay hid in their hearts to be brought forth. The smoke of a great furnace. The doctrine of Antichrist is rightly called smoke because Antichrist himself is the furnace purging the good and reducing the wicked to ashes. The sun and the air were darkened. And thereby some were struck who enlighten others, and some enlightened by them.
9.3: 9.3 There came out locusts. The disciples of the heretics are compared to locusts, because they neither fly on high, or, contemplate through knowledge, nor walk firmly by good working: but leap by pride, and fall back into worse, and are gnawers of the good. As scorpions have. The scorpion, fair of face, stings secretly with the tail; or he compares to the scorpion because as the scorpion with the tail, so heretics deceive by temporal things, which ought to be afterward, as the tail is the hinder part in an animal. Or he compares so because when the scorpion stings it is not felt, afterward it diffuses venom, so those deceived by heretics do not feel it, at length perish.
9.4: 9.4 It was commanded them that they should not hurt, etc. Because God restrains the wiles of these, though they themselves understand not.
9.5: 9.5 That they should not kill. When by wiles heretics cannot overthrow in some matter they wish to, against them it is ordained by God that although they kill bodies, they should not deceive souls. Five months. Another reading says six months, on account of the six ages by which this life is distinguished. As the torment of a scorpion. Though power is given to torment, they do not torment openly, but accuse before the princes of the world.
9.6: 9.6 And death shall flee from them. Because the care of the flock binds them to labor.
9.7: 9.7 The shapes of the locusts, etc. Having shown how they harm, both by wiles and by hidden assault, and in both the restraint of God, now he shows what sort they are through whom they can work. Like horses. Because they are swift to run about, fierce to assail, and foresee not whom they run into, whether neighbors or enemies. As crowns. That is of victories gained over the headlong and overthrown, not through true wisdom.
9.8: 9.8 And they had hair. That is wanton and effeminate manners, which cling to them, and hang from them for the deception of others. Or the hairs are lesser men, whom, clinging to themselves, they deceive. Teeth of lions. They have mangling and stench.
9.9: 9.9 Breastplates. That is obstinate hearts, which the arrow of truth does not pierce. Or opinions fortified by deceptions, which truth breaks. As the noise of chariots, etc. Diverse chariots by diverse ways and by diverse horses are hurried to the same battle, so these by diverse heresies unanimously assail the Church.
9.10: 9.10 And they had tails. When their reason or tumult avails not, they seek the help of princes, who are called tails, because to constrain, they terrify and flatter. Or the tails are deceitful opinions, with which before the face they flatter and secretly sting.
9.11: 9.11 And they had over them a king. Having shown what sort they are in themselves, he shows through whom they can do these things. Whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon. As if to say: Beware of this, you Hebrews, Greeks and Latins, that is the whole Church. He put three tongues, because the Gospel of Christ is written and received in one of these three tongues.
9.12: 9.12 One woe is past. That is the first in the order of narration and the order of time. For this is the declaration and damnation of the evils that will be in the time of Antichrist.
9.13: 9.13 From the four horns. By the four horns understand those four things which are preached of Christ, which are the nativity, passion, resurrection, and ascension: around which the others are. Of the golden altar. The altar is Christ, the horns of the altar are the preachers lifting up Christ, and ready to die for him, as the blood was placed on the horns of the altar. Or the altar is the Church, in which are the horns, that is defenders of others, who all tend to the same. Or by the four horns we can understand the evangelical dogmas which teach that the frauds of Antichrist be detected. One voice. The heralds of past time forewarn those who will be in the time of Antichrist.
9.14: 9.14 Loose the four. For the four parts of the world, or because they assail the four things preached of Christ. Who are bound in the great river Euphrates. The Euphrates is a river going round Babylon, that is the worldly princes through whom the devil, while he was in them, worked secretly. Saying loose, he commands them to be excommunicated, that he who was in them as it were bound, may work more openly through them delivered to him. Or the four angels are all the unclean spirits reigning in the four parts of the world, who were restrained in the passion of Christ.
9.15: 9.15 Were loosed, etc. The devil loosed, many are cast down, who endeavor to blind others. For an hour and a day. By hour take half a year; by day, one year; by month, another year; and by year, a third: for three years and a half the persecution of Antichrist will last.
9.16: 9.16 Twenty thousand times ten thousand. The saints perfect by the ten precepts of the law, against whom a double number of the wicked is set, because the wicked are more than the good. And I heard, etc. As if to say: Well do I put it under a fixed number, because I heard, that is understood, that the wicked were more than the good.
9.17: 9.17 And thus I saw. That is as I had understood that they rode to the destruction of others, so he understood that they did this through the devil, whom as horses they carried, or the horses can be understood as devils, upon whom the wicked are founded. They had fiery breastplates. That is they fortified them with opinions from which follows eternal punishment, where is fire and stench and smoke. Or they had fiery breastplates, that is eternal punishment, which never lets go those it takes. As the heads of lions. Above in the plague of the locusts he saw faces of men, here of lions: because heretics show something of humanity, but the ministers of Antichrist, what they shall teach by words and signs, this they will also by punishments compel to confess. Out of their mouths proceeded fire. The cause of eternal punishment. Or fire, that is cupidity; smoke, that is pride; brimstone, that is the stench of evil works. Smoke and brimstone. They are blind and set in darkness, on account of the stench of vices and evil works.
9.18: 9.18 The third part was killed. That is all the reprobate of the Church, and likewise all Jews or pagans, who were never baptized, nor separated from the Church.
9.19: 9.19 Like to serpents. Who flatter with the face, and secretly inject poison.
10.1: 10.1 And I saw another mighty angel. Because the strong armed man overcame the strong devil. From heaven. That is by the knowledge of angels. Clothed with a cloud. That is humbling himself by taking flesh, or because he made himself knowable. Hiding in the flesh, which is refreshment to us against vices. And a rainbow on his head. He who has true knowledge of God reckons him to be God. As a pillar of fire. Those in whom the image of God truly shines, as in contemplatives, or preaching.
10.2: 10.2 And he had in his hand a little book open. That is all the Scriptures fulfilled by his work, partly by preaching, partly by fulfilling what was said of himself: at last opening the sense to his own. His foot. That is carriers firm in faith and sustaining others. The left on the earth. That is upon those who in any way sustained, though they did not believe. That is: he placed the greater and firmer preachers over the greater sinners, the lesser over the lesser.
10.3: 10.3 As when a lion roars. The voice of the lion shows his strength and brings terror. When the lion with his tail makes a furrow round the wood and roars, none of the wild beasts dares to come out: so Christ, shutting his own in the faith, roars that none go out.
10.4: 10.4 I was about to write. Here he bears the person of those who in the time of Antichrist will wish to preach in imitation of those before. The things which the seven thunders spoke: divine inspiration, or angelic admonition.
10.5: 10.5 Lifted up his hand to heaven. When there shall be so great desolation in the Church that even preaching will be taken away; lest the faithful despair, they hear for their consolation that preaching is withdrawn not to the detriment of their salvation.
10.6: 10.6 Swore, etc. And thereby firmly established that he was God: For if Christ is risen, we also shall rise, 1 Corinthians 15. And the things that are in it. When you say: He created the things that are in it, he destroyed the heresy of some who assert that certain things were not created by God but by the demon, such as the toad. Time shall be no longer. That is no variety, but eternal stability, immortality of souls. These last considering this will suffer willingly.
10.7: 10.7 Shall be finished the mystery. In the time of Antichrist, so great will be the persecution that preaching will be forbidden to those who shall be in his time, though they wish to preach, even if they are to have the office of preaching from their predecessors; others, however, preached the same, because they were instituted to this by Christ. Christ instituted them, because then was the time of preaching, and he had come for this, but now see the destruction of the time of Antichrist contrary to the destruction which Christ made, and thereby weigh that preaching is deservedly withdrawn. The mystery of God. That is the reward of the saints, which is a secret, which eye has not seen nor ear heard, 1 Corinthians 2.
10.8: 10.8 As he has declared. The prophets' first intention was about the coming of the Lord, and the consummation of the world.
10.9: 10.9 And I heard. As if to say: The destruction that will be in the time of Antichrist having been shown, and preaching withdrawn thence, and for this comfort applied to the faithful, he is admonished to preach meanwhile what he has seen, as if it were said to him plainly: Behold I have revealed all things to you, now go and preach, nor because they are harsh, avoid them: nor be terrified at any tribulation, because you will not suffer as much as those will suffer who shall persevere in the time of Antichrist. This is put here for the consolation of the present Church, where the greater tribulation is pronounced. Go. What he knew well, he is admonished to understand, that by the admonition others who will preach may be informed. Standing upon the sea. He says this because to fulfill it is grave to humanity, which is soft and frail.
10.10: 10.10 And I went. He says this, because God, if he sees one ready, freely offers what is necessary. To the angel. That is to the Scripture fulfilled by God, intimated by the faithful.
10.11: 10.11 And he said to me: You must, etc. When I received the book, though I understood bitter things, he admonished that I not abandon it even for death.
11.1: 11.1 Measure. That is, so preach according to the capacity of each, that you establish the Church and in it the altar, etc.
11.2: 11.2 The court. That is false Christians, who feign themselves the Church, but deny it by deeds. The holy city. That is the Church gathered to live justly, and imbued with virtues, they shall persecute forty-two months, that is three years and a half, in which Antichrist shall reign; as if to say: Know that all the persecutions that are in the present, and that were in the past, proceed from Antichrist, like those which will be in his own time.
11.3: 11.3 And I will give to my two. As if to say: When the tribulation is less, you ought not to cease, because in the time when it shall be graver, I will make them preach. Two witnesses. It is of Elijah and Enoch, through whom other preachers are understood. A thousand days. Note that these days do not complete three years and a half, as Christ also did not complete half a year of his preaching beyond three years.
11.6: 11.6 Over the waters. That is over the doctrines, which are waters watering to the faithful. Into blood, etc. Into sin, either when what is heard is neglected, or when to be heard is even despised.
11.8: 11.8 Egypt. That is the dark, without knowledge of God.
11.10: 11.10 And shall send gifts. That is gifts, literally: or congratulations and chattings among themselves speaking of them.
11.11: 11.11 And after days. Having shown their tribulation, by whose example the angel invited John to preach, even if it is necessary to suffer with them: he shows yet their crowns also, that he may likewise make this John, or any other, certain of his crown according to his measure. Upon their feet. That is upon themselves who before were in need of something to lean on, but then will be firm.
11.12: 11.12 A great voice. Which may refresh them and terrify enemies.
11.13: 11.13 A great earthquake. That is the earthly were moved, that they be punished in hell; or for the destruction of the Church, the masters being slain. And the tenth part. That is man, who seems appointed for this, that the tenth order be restored. Were killed in the earthquake. Wholly destroyed in hell, or afterward repented not. Glory to God. That is praises to God for the salvation of the just and the damnation of the wicked.
11.15: 11.15 And the seventh angel, etc. The six former trumpets, compared to the ages of the present world, announced various onsets of the battles of the Church; but the seventh, herald of the eternal sabbath, shows only the victory and empire of the true King. It is done. He who before was vile and abject now reigns, crowning the good and condemning the wicked. And he shall reign. That is his kingdom shall abide forever, not as some heretics think that the saints after a set time will return to the life of the world.
11.16: 11.16 And the twenty-four ancients. Not only the lesser so glorify God, but also the greater. Fell on their faces. He falls on his face who in this life acknowledges his fault and bewails it by penance. He falls backward who in this life falls suddenly, and knows not to what punishments he is led.
11.18: 11.18 Who corrupted the earth. That is themselves by evil working, and others by evil example.
11.19: 11.19 And it was opened. In this fourth vision you have matter well adorned and having good helps, namely concerning the fight of the Church which is assailed by the devil both openly and secretly, and in all these John shows she overcomes, by which he chiefly arms the faithful that they fail not in any tribulation. Knowledge of the fight of the Church therefore depends on the third vision, which is about the enjoined office of preaching. The temple of God was opened, that is the Holy Spirit was given, by whom the mysteries of the Church, which were figured by the second tabernacle, are revealed to the faithful. The ark. Christ is the ark in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden, who fulfilled the Old Testament and instituted the New. And great hail. That is to some preaching seemed intolerable.
12.1: 12.1 And a sign. And from these I saw this proceed, namely the grace of faith, signifying something great. Here he makes mention of the revelation of mysteries which were in the second vision, and of the enjoined office of preaching, which we had in the third, that he may show that this fourth, which is of the fight of the Church and the devil, depends on these two, that is the second and third. The moon under her feet. Though the Church be sustained by worldly things, she affects them not. And on her head a crown, etc. That is the twelve apostles, whom the world believed, or in whom the Church conquered the world.
12.2: 12.2 She is in pain to be delivered. By preaching, she suffers adversities. Or she is tormented by herself, that is she mortifies her flesh, that preaching may be fit.
12.3: 12.3 A great dragon. He speaks not of great effect but of the power and pride of the dragon. And ten horns, etc. That is the kingdoms and riches with which princes assail the decalogue of the law.
12.4: 12.4 And his tail. That is deceptions, with which they hide vices, as base things are hidden by the tail. Of the stars. That is of those who enlighten the Church by doctrine, not by life. Stood before the woman. Who was suffering pain, through which he believed she would soon cease. Through the passion the devil believed the Church was subdued. Devour. The dragon was ready to devour; but could not, because he was born who forbade.
12.5: 12.5 And she brought forth. By carnal generation Christ came forth from Abraham and David; or the Church brought forth a son, that is the faith of Christ in the hearts of hearers.
12.6: 12.6 A thousand days. That is the whole time in which the Church subsists, made by the preaching of Christ for three years and a half.
12.7: 12.7 Michael and his angels fought. Sustaining the Church by praying, bringing help.
12.8: 12.8 They prevailed not. To remove the help of the angels, because they will not be able to lead the Church into sin.
12.10: 12.10 And I heard a voice. When he had shown the devil in this hidden contest conquered by the Church with the help of the Son and the angels, he adds the exultations of the angels themselves, or of the holy souls over the victory of the brethren, that they may strive to conquer who hear that angels or holy souls rejoice at their victory. Accused them. The office of the devil is to accuse, that is to make accusable through sin. Day and night. In prosperity by delighting, in adversity by saddening.
12.12: 12.12 The devil is come down. From heaven: or from the lesser saints, in whom temptation has no place now. Knowing that he has but a short time. Because he sees many withdrawn from him and put in his place. And after he saw. When the devil saw that he could not prosper by hidden fraud, he undertakes to assault by open tribulation. And there were given to the woman, etc. Who also against open tribulation has help from the same Son from whom she had against hidden assault.
12.14: 12.14 Of an eagle. Those are called eagles who by the conversation of life seek heaven, and therefore have a fixed gaze on God. For a time, and times, etc. If the state of that Church which will be in the time of Antichrist is understood, it will be said otherwise, for a time and times and half a time, etc., for the preaching of Elijah and Enoch; if the general time of the Church is understood, it is said, for a time, and times, and half a time, etc., otherwise, for the preaching of Christ made for three years and a half, because by the preaching of Christ the Church is fed daily.
12.16: 12.16 And the earth helped the woman. That is Christ gave his Church strength to suffer. And opened, that is prepared and made herself fit, to receive whatever they brought on her, like one opening the mouth. This Christ did in his passion, in which he set himself before his own as an example of suffering. Swallowed up, that is destroyed in himself all the punishments, being made immortal and impassible, which the same he does in his own.
12.17: 12.17 The dragon was angry against the woman. Because although he cannot conquer her, yet he does not cease to envy, and to seek a place of attack.
12.18: 12.18 And he stood. Yet he did not conquer all the lesser, but only upon the sand, that is, he made delay among the unfruitful, in whom signs of the footprint appear.
13.1: 13.1 And I saw, etc. This beast is spiritually Antichrist, or generally the whole collection of the wicked. Seven heads and ten horns. That he might be able well to overcome these, he established such a household for himself. Names of blasphemy. The beast was full of various heresies, or hiding vices with various pretenses.
13.3: 13.3 As it were slain. Antichrist will feign himself dead, and lying hid three days will afterward appear, saying he is raised. And his death's wound was healed. By magic art he will ascend into the air, the demons carrying him, and so his death's wound will be healed, because before he was believed dead, afterward he will be reputed living.
13.6: 13.6 And he opened his mouth. He broke out into such confidence that what he did secretly before, he then dares to blaspheme publicly. And his tabernacle. That is all his institution, through which he appears praiseworthy.
13.8: 13.8 Slain from the beginning of the world, in his own, as in Abel. Or because it was arranged before all things that he would be slain at the end of times. Or he was slain in the lamb mystically which Abel offered, or in Abel himself, slain by his brother, he was prefigured.
13.10: 13.10 He that shall lead into captivity. He who captivates men now from faith, at length from salvation, namely Antichrist, or the devil himself. He that shall kill by the sword. Antichrist and his shall kill with the material sword and with persuasion, and shall perish by the sword of the eternal judgment. Here is, etc. That is, the saints shall hold patience and faith, because, he being destroyed, they know they will be rewarded. Looking at the punishment of the wicked and the reward of the good, they become patient and hold the faith.
13.11: 13.11 And I saw. The tribulation having been described which will be through Antichrist and his partakers, he adds another which will be through his apostles whom he will scatter throughout the whole world. Horns. Because they will feign to have the innocence, and pure life, and true doctrine, and miracles, which Christ had and gave to his own; or, they will usurp the two Testaments to themselves. And he spoke as a dragon. That is the false apostles will speak as the devil had spoken in Antichrist.
13.12: 13.12 And he exercised the power, etc. Because in all things they set Antichrist as their head before themselves. The earth. That is the earthly, and those persevering in love of the earth; or: the earth according to the body, dwelling in it according to the soul. To adore. Because these also, feigning resurrection, make it the foundation of their preaching, as the apostles of Christ also did.
13.13: 13.13 Fire, that is the malignant spirit he will cause to descend upon his own, that they speak with various tongues. As to the apostles the Holy Spirit was given in the form of fire, so those will give the malignant spirit in the form of fire. In the sight. That all may be able to see as when the apostles received the Holy Spirit in the upper room.
13.15: 13.15 That the image should speak. Here by magic art he will make the statue speak and foretell the future.
13.16: 13.16 To have a character, etc. In the hand and on the forehead they will put signs, that all may confess their god by word and deed.
13.17: 13.17 The number. That is those who expect from him a reward, the smaller, or middling, or greatest.
13.18: 13.18 He that has. Since the present book was published in Greek, the number is to be sought according to the Greeks, among whom all letters signify a number. His name Antemos, which fits him who is called contrary to Christ: A, one; N, fifty; T, four hundred; E, five; M, forty; O, seventy; S, two hundred. Or Arnoyme, that is I deny, who denies Christ God, in which the same number: A, one; R, two hundred; N, fifty; O, seventy; Y, four hundred; M, forty; E, five. Or Teitan, that is sun giant, which agrees with the true Christ, usurpatively with Antichrist: T, three hundred; E, five; I, ten; again T, three hundred; A, one; N, fifty. Or with Latin letters: Diclux, because he will say himself to be light: D, five hundred; I, one; C, one hundred; L, fifty; V, five; X, ten; and so the same sum. Six is the first perfect number, and signifies the less perfect who are married, and according to their measure keep the ten precepts. Sixty signifies the moderately perfect, who, having left lawful marriages, remain in chastity, and again fulfill the ten precepts according to their measure. One hundred signifies the most perfect who do not violate the integrity of mind and body and keep the ten precepts most perfectly. These render fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, some a hundredfold. And the disciples of Antichrist will then say that no one can be saved unless they offer something of those fruits to Antichrist.
14.1: 14.1 And I saw: and behold the Lamb stood. The gravest persecution having been shown which the Church will suffer from Antichrist and his apostles, now he shows what helper she has, and what household he himself has, that he may the more console the afflicted elect. A hundred forty-four, etc. That is the most perfect in virginity, gathered in the faith of the Trinity from the four parts of the world.
14.2: 14.2 Of thunder. Because it terrifies those who flee from coming into his fellowship. Of harpers. Because they have so instituted themselves that they stretch their devout hearts upon the wood of the cross. Harping on their harps. What they had by office, they fulfilled in work.
14.3: 14.3 And they sung. That is they will exult over the integrity of soul and body: which joy shall never grow old to them, but is always to them as new.
14.4: 14.4 These are they who are not defiled with women. That is those whom the blood of Christ raised up to be virgins. First-fruits from among men, etc. As the best horse from the herd, or the first-fruits from the fruits.
14.6: 14.6 And I saw. The assault made by the two beasts having been described, and the help of the Lamb and the dignity of his household shown, an admonition is added, that they approach this household, and a threat, that they turn aside from the other. Another angel. That is the preachers who are other than Christ, that is carrying out his office. Through the midst of heaven. Through the Catholic Church, which they draw with them by words and examples. The eternal gospel. That is the preaching promising eternal things, and leading its observers to eternity.
14.7: 14.7 Fear the Lord, etc. By working well, and announcing him well, that through you he may appear glorious. Because he is come. As if to say: Do not fail, for you will not suffer for a long time.
14.8: 14.8 And another angel followed. He says this, because preachers succeed one another. Is fallen. The word fallen set twice signifies infinity, in which every kind of destruction is understood. Of the wine of the wrath of her fornication. That is, of vices, and chiefly idolatry, which is a sweet drink to sinners, with which they themselves defile others, and make them drunk so they walk not the right path; whence the wrath of God is owed to them. Pure wine is drunk, when God scourges here for amendment: turbid, when eternal damnation is inflicted.
14.9: 14.9 And the third angel. He puts three for the faith of the Trinity, since these three can be considered in the same person.
14.10: 14.10 Which is mixed. As if he said: He who is not corrected, his vengeance given for correction, will be punished with eternal punishment. In the cup. The cup is the vengeance of God, where above is the pure wine which he avenges here for correction, below is the dregs, that is damnation in the last things.
