The wicked will drink of the wine, that is of the dregs: which wine, because he wishes to show it turbid by comparison with the pure, he adds that it is mixed.
14.11: 14.11 And the smoke of their torments. That he enumerates some things of the damnation of the wicked, he does not say to describe the damnation: but only to bring terror to those whom he deters from their fellowship. Shall ascend for ever and ever. When he says: shall ascend forever, he notes that eternal punishment is continued. Nor have they rest. As if: No wonder if those who adored Antichrist in his time are punished, because his ministers also before them will have the same punishment.
14.12: 14.12 Here is the patience, etc. That is here the saints ought to suffer patiently, lest they come to eternal punishment.
14.13: 14.13 Works. That is the rewards of the works which follow. As if: While they were in the world, greater tribulations came upon them for a greater crown: whence they were reputed so abject, but now they shall suffer nothing.
14.14: 14.14 And I saw. The reward of the good having been shown, by which he invited to their fellowship, he adds the damnation of the impious, that through terror he may lead to the same purpose. Like to the Son of man. Because he who is immortal was now no longer truly the Son of man.
14.15: 14.15 An angel. That is the saints, who until now had been hidden among the faithful, will appear in brightness as about to judge, praying with desire that God make the separation of the good and the wicked. Came out of the temple. The saints are said to come out of the temple when they now appear not such as they once were, but such as they will remain forever. For the hour is come, etc. Because it is now fitting, when the number of yours is complete.
14.18: 14.18 And another angel, etc. When Saint John had shown that God, who has the power of judging, is implored by the saints, and so the judgment is made, he shows that the saints have the same power, and that Christ commands them to judge, and they obey the command. Another angel, that is Christ, who had been hidden and vile, appeared bright among the faithful, and coming from the altar, that is from a more secret place, which never other saints, for Christ alone is known by all as consubstantial with God. Put in your sickle. By the harvest of the earth and the grapes of the vineyard, the damnation of the same wicked is understood; yet by the vineyard we have more precisely those who worked evil with greater zeal, as vineyards, to bear fruit greater care is applied than to the earth.
14.19: 14.19 And he cast into the winepress, etc. Whence the Prophet: A pit wherein is no water, that is refreshment.
14.20: 14.20 And the blood came out. Eternal punishment for the sin of blood, but not the wine which is in the cellar of God is put. Even to the horses' bridles, that is even to the very rulers of the wicked to be punished, namely the devils. For a thousand six hundred furlongs. Understand all detained by the games of the world, that is by vices, who either simply are perfect in this, which we have by six; or more perfect, which by a hundred; or most perfect, which by a thousand.
15.1: 15.1 And I saw, etc. In these three visions above said, that is the revelation of mysteries, the giving of trumpets, and in the fight of the woman against the devil, he has followed the order from the beginning of redemption to the day of judgment: but in these three following he dwells on the last times, because of the preceding things in other divine Scriptures it has been said more clearly, but of those little and more hiddenly. In this fifth vision therefore, the matter is seven angels holding vials, in which are contained the plagues, that is the destructions of the wicked who shall be in the time of Antichrist, which destruction chiefly exhorts those present to suffer. In what follows he puts three visions, though there are four above. But the first omitted, which was about the correction of the churches, he speaks of the other three, with consideration however. And wonderful. It is wonderful that a man should have so great power as to be able to damn others. Seven plagues, that is all, the blinding and destruction of those who shall be in the time of Antichrist. For in them. Truly they will have plagues, because they will exercise the wrath of God upon the wicked, and truly the last, because in the world after them God will bring no others.
15.2: 15.2 As it were a sea of glass mingled with fire. That is baptism, where purity of faith is required, and men are cleansed from vices. Having harps, that is mortifying the flesh, which God enjoined on them, or which he first did himself.
15.3: 15.3 The canticle of Moses. That is the old law, and it is exultation to those who understand well, that is spiritually. The ways, that is the institutions of God, by which we come to God, or he to us, are just, because they render to each according to merit; and true, because they lead where they promise.
15.4: 15.4 Your judgments, etc. That you choose some, reprobate others, that the faithful may know it is from justice.
15.5: 15.5 And after these things. When they had shown those angels to have power to strike, about to say what plagues they are to bring, he first sets the cause by which he shows them worthy to suffer the plagues, namely that all the mysteries of the Church are revealed to all willing to enter, which these cannot understand by their own evil merit. The temple was opened, that is the mysteries of the Church were revealed, in which God dwells, and they fight for the honor of God.
15.6: 15.6 And they came out. And because they were so open, preachers will come out and reprove evil-doers.
15.7: 15.7 And one. Because what they will preach they will have from the institution of the former fathers, who are all called one, because they teach one thing. Of wrath, that is anger: because they correct, rebuke, threaten the wrath of God to sinners, and sometimes also excommunicate.
15.8: 15.8 Smoke from the majesty, etc. Although then all things will be so open to the faithful, yet they themselves will be closed and obscure to the unbelieving. To enter, that is to understand that hidden judgment of God, why he chose some, reprobates others, until at the end of the world the saints shall openly know. Or, to enter meanwhile into the Church, until the full damnation of the wicked be completed in judgment, because afterward it is plain they will not enter.
16.2: 16.2 A sore. Disobedience is the cause why that sore is made.
16.3: 16.3 And it became blood. That is his damnation was brought on for the blood which they shed. Blood, that is that damnation will be as of a dead man, that is irrevocable; for as a dead man returns not to life, so that sentence of damnation will not be revoked. Every living soul. All who consent, who seem to live, not because they openly persecute, but for consent, will be damned.
16.4: 16.4 Upon the rivers, etc. Because likewise these will be damned for the blood they shed, either bodily or spiritually.
16.5: 16.5 I heard. That is I understood the very preachers who will do this vengeance, ascribing it not to themselves but to the Lord, and confirming that it is done justly. Who art and who wast. He does not put the one who is to come, because he understood he would come soon.
16.6: 16.6 And thou hast given them blood to drink. That is, eternal punishment for the shedding of blood, in earning which they delighted.
16.7: 16.7 And I heard. What the masters say, the disciples confirm. Yea, O Lord God almighty, etc. From great affection they turn the speech to God. Just. For it is just that he who shed blood drink the vengeance of blood.
16.9: 16.9 And they were scorched. Or the afflicted will afflict their tormentors with the heat of anger, as they will be found inseparable, and so they were scorched with envy and wrath. Neither did they. Inwardly repenting they grieved, outwardly they dared not confess.
16.10: 16.10 Upon the seat of the beast. He says this, because these are only bodies, and not spirits: upon whom he will sit, because he will give bodily and not spiritual things. They gnawed, etc. Refreshing themselves all by mutual detraction.
16.12: 16.12 That the way might be prepared. Because, the world finished, there will be the resurrection of the faithful, who shall come from the rising of the sun, that is from Christ, when he begins to shine, that is to manifest himself.
16.13: 16.13 I saw. The pouring of the vial upon these, and themselves not corrected, but cast down into greater blindness. Spirits to come out. That is all the impious who for excess of malice are to be called unclean spirits; or, the demons themselves, whom they beget in the hearts of others. For as the faithful by their doctrine beget the faith of Christ in the hearts of others, so these by malice the devil. Of frogs. Frogs dwell in mud, and are talkative, and take away rest from others: so also these.
16.14: 16.14 They go forth, etc. The demons go forth, and the devil will gather, because all are one.
16.16: 16.16 And he shall gather. That is they will make them have trust in Antichrist, who is the refuge for all wishing to steal their faith from the saints; or to whom all the wicked of diverse sects will boast.
16.17: 16.17 And the seventh angel. Having shown upon whom the angels pour out their vials, he adds what befalls these wicked by that pouring, namely that here as far as they can they will resist, as if from the very pouring they received increase, but at length they will be thrust down into hell.
16.18: 16.18 And the city. Because of this damnation and because of the sins that they add, the city itself is damned, and the punishment is divided to each according to merit, to Jews namely and Gentiles and false Christians. The cities of the nations fell, that is all the collections of the wicked remaining in the first generation will be damned: carnal, not in the second spiritual regeneration.
16.19: 16.19 Came in remembrance. That is God remembered the single sins of those whom before he seemed to have forgotten. To give her the cup. That God himself might give them punishment measured for the delights they had. God renders to the wicked according to their deserts, that is what they deserved, but not as much as they deserved, so that in the very retribution where justice is plain there may be mercy also. For all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth. To the good also he gives according to merit and more than they deserved, that mercy may prevail over justice there.
16.20: 16.20 And every island fled away. And he saw that all who were afflicted for God in the world and eminent in virtues, in respect of these punishments, in their life shunned the fellowship of the impious, and therefore were not found in their punishments.
16.21: 16.21 A talent. There are three kinds of talent: great, of a hundred and twenty pounds; middle, of seventy-two; less, fifty. Of the middle he speaks here, because sinners in the seventy-two tongues shall not escape this vengeance. And blasphemed. That is, set in hell, although they know they are punished according to merit, they will grieve that God has such power as to bring plagues on them, and it is blasphemy.
17.1: 17.1 And there came one, etc. When he had described the plagues which preachers will bring in the time of Antichrist, and the eternal damnation which the same impious will suffer, he admonishes to attend to the causes of that damnation. As if: I have shown you what will be in that future, now beware, you powerful, because the same devil who then will deceive so openly, deceives secretly every day, and will lead you to the same ruin as them. Angels. The angel here has the person of the teacher, John holds the person of the learner. I will show you the damnation, that is the cause of the damnation of the wicked, who, leaving the Creator, fornicate with the demon, by worshiping idols, loving earthly things, serving uncleanness. The harlot. This great harlot is Antichrist, and the wicked who shall be in his time; who already sits upon waters, that is already reigns over the powerful wicked, of whom all he is the head. Who sits upon many waters, that is, who reigns over many peoples whom luxury draws to herself. Whence the Lord to Job: His strength, Job 40., namely of the devil, is in his loins, when he deceives men (whose seed is in the loins): in the navel, when he deceives women (whose seed is in the navel). Whence the Prophet in Ezekiel 16, to Jerusalem as to a harlot: In the day of your birth, that is at this time of the world, your navel was not cut, that is, you have not restrained luxury.
17.2: 17.2 Have been made drunk, etc. As a drunkard fears nothing, so those clinging to earthly things will be so blinded by love of the earth that they neither love God nor fear punishments.
17.3: 17.3 A woman sitting. That is those soft ones who are conformed to Eve (from whom sin began); who have the devil as foundation, who is bloody both in himself and in his own; or because they shed the blood of the saints, they misunderstand the utterances of God. Seven heads. The five senses of the body, and afterward error, and at length Antichrist, through which seven the devil leads men to sin. Ten horns. That is the ten kingdoms which will be in the time of Antichrist, by which others are understood.
17.4: 17.4 Clothed round about with purple. That is with the royal garment: they will say they are kings that they may deceive. With gold. Because they will seem enlightened by divine wisdom. A golden cup, that is the divine Scripture, with which the faithful are given to drink for salvation. Abomination. That is, which, according to those expositions, ought to be cast away by men, because they teach uncleanness of the flesh and fornication from God.
17.5: 17.5 And on her forehead. Though she is so apt to deceive, yet, O faithful, despair not, for she has on her forehead, that is in the manifest, the sign which to the unskilled is a mystery, by which she gives an example of committing sins, for which earthly men are repelled from the salvation of the faithful.
17.6: 17.6 Drunk. That is pressed down by vengeance for the shedding of blood: that for excess of sorrows she knows not where she is. And I wondered. Here John takes the person of those who, when they see the wicked exalted in the world, wonder when they hear the punishments that are promised to those same wicked, and since they are to be so punished, why God permits them to be exalted. But they are taught to understand that exaltation is given for greater blinding, and at length eternal damnation is justly brought on.
17.7: 17.7 I will tell thee. That is why these wicked are punished, that is the devil who made them sin: which is unknown, except to the learned.
17.8: 17.8 Of the beast that carries her. The beast, that is the devil, carries, that is rules, the woman, that is all the wicked effeminate. For he who rules others is said to bear as it were the burden of rule. Was. Before the coming of Christ, the devil had the greatest power, but after, though he did not wholly lose it, yet he has it not a little weakened. Shall ascend. Because in the time of Antichrist he will receive power, for through those who are in the depths of sin he will ascend into elation. And shall go into destruction. Because, Antichrist being dead, he will have no more place for tempting. Shall wonder. When the wicked see their power so annihilated, they will grieve: not as repenting, but only wondering. Seven heads. By these seven the devil lifts men into pride, and in these the unbelievers lean.
17.10: 17.10 Five are fallen. Adam, had he persevered in obedience, the senses of the body would be turned to no pleasure, namely evil; but through sin they were so corrupted that it is now natural to seek soft things by touch, savory by taste, fragrant by smell, beautiful by sight. These are the five kings through whom the devil rules in childhood, because he was the cause why they were corrupted. These are the five husbands of the Samaritan woman. In youth error succeeds, for after he has discretion, and if he sins, it is imputed now not to the senses but to error: of which the Lord: He whom you now have is not your husband, John 4.
17.11: 17.11 Of the seven. Because likewise he sins, and likewise will be punished: and the eighth itself, because it surpasses all, both in wickedness and in punishment.
17.15: 17.15 Are peoples, etc., that is the present wicked, gathered from all diversity of men.
17.16: 17.16 Shall make her desolate. The solace of the devil is the destruction of the wicked, whom he will destroy when the number of the impious is complete. And naked. The devil has power of doing signs to deceive, this he will lose when the number of the good is complete, because afterward temptation will have no place. Flesh. They are said to eat the flesh of the harlot, because they will delight in the punishments to be inflicted. Shall burn with fire. That is, they shall be tormented for her delights which they followed.
17.17: 17.17 Until the words be fulfilled. Of the promise of rewards or punishments.
18.1: 18.1 And after these things I saw. In this sixth vision, he treats of the last punishments which the impious will suffer in hell for each sin; and first he shows about Babylon; afterward about the beast and false prophets; at length about the devil himself in whom the end is plain, in whose damnation will be the end. This damnation he is about to follow up, and says it was preached by Christ, that greater faith may be had in it.
18.2: 18.2 Is fallen, is fallen. Twice for the double damnation of soul and body, or because it will be punished eternally. The hold of every unclean spirit. The demons in perverse hearts are unclean for the allurements of the flesh, are birds through elation of mind, or because they run through this air.
18.3: 18.3 Of the power. That is of the sins by which riches are acquired, because every rich man is either unjust, or heir of an unjust man.
18.4: 18.4 And I heard. Saying that damnation to come to those present, he adds an admonition. Go out, because little time remains in which they shall receive reward according to merit.
18.5: 18.5 For her sins have reached, etc. Sins reach even to contempt of God through impenitence.
18.6: 18.6 Render to her. As my vengeance has been exercised on you who are purged, so avenge my injury on them. Double the double, that is bring on soul and body greater punishments than they brought on you.
18.7: 18.7 As much as she has glorified herself, etc. This is rightly said, because some receive more, some less. For the cause of this discernment he repeats what he had said above. And I am not a widow. Because I have consolation in temporal things.
18.8: 18.8 Death. Absence of life, that is of God, because his presence is life.
18.9: 18.9 And shall weep. But others shall have everlasting joy. The kings of the earth. Even those who ruled their earthliness well; but sometimes fornicated with it, will grieve that they never were like those. When they shall see the smoke of her burning, that is, when riches fail, which is a sign of the eternal burning of judgment; or when they shall see punishment exalted beyond measure.
18.11: 18.11 And the merchants of the earth shall weep. Because they will grieve that those things perish in which they reckoned their prosperity.
18.12: 18.12 Of gold and silver, etc. By gold wisdom, silver the divine utterances. Christ is signified in the precious stone; the apostles in pearls: in white linen the justifications of the saints; in purple martyrdom; in silk virginity; in scarlet charity; in thyine wood, incorruptible, unfailing constancy; in ivory the beauty of virtues; in brass strength and longanimity; in iron the sharpness of loftiness; in marble invincible humility.
18.13: 18.13 Cinnamon. In cinnamon should be understood the odor of the virtues which they feign. Of fine flour and wheat, that is the flesh of Christ, with which the faithful are truly satisfied, the reprobate are provoked. Of slaves and souls. He distinguishes: because some become servants only in body, as Joseph; some also in mind, as if an Egyptian sold to a Jew be circumcised after their rite, or worship the idols of the pagans.
18.20: 18.20 Rejoice over her. After he foretold this damnation to come on the impious, he admonishes the good to rejoice, that they may agree with the divine judgment; or because, these being damned, their reward follows.
18.21: 18.21 And took up. God lifts up the wicked that he may punish more gravely or that they may fall. A stone like a great millstone. Literally all these things were seen. With this violence. After the single punishments were described, the manner of damnation is shown to himself, as if he said: What I saw foretold I saw also already fulfilled, as you see in this figure; or: the more they were exalted, the more gravely they will fall.
19.1: 19.1 After these things I heard. That is, I saw the damnation of the wicked completed, as I had heard from Christ it was to be completed. Now he adds that the saints exult over this damnation as they had been admonished to exult in that verse: Rejoice over her, O heaven, by which the punishment of the wicked is understood to be much graver. Alleluia, etc. Therefore we say alleluia, because it is praise to our God, and because he has done such things for us, we ought to praise him excellently.
19.4: 19.4 And the ancients fell down, etc. Not only the lesser saints praised God for this damnation, but also those greater ones who were judges and teachers of others in the Church. Amen. Specially God is to be praised for this, that he so punishes our enemies.
19.5: 19.5 And a voice, etc. The damnation of the wicked and the exultation of the saints having been told, he adds an admonition to those present, as if to say: You have seen the exultation, now provide for yourselves for your salvation. The small. Those who cannot penetrate the higher mysteries, nor fulfill the counsel of God: Sell all and follow me, are understood by the name of the small.
19.6: 19.6 And I heard as it were the voice, etc. The joy which the saints had over the perdition of the wicked having been shown, he adds another joy of theirs which they will have for their own salvation (of which he is about to speak).
19.7: 19.7 And his wife, etc. And it is fitting that the Church be joined to Christ, because the Church herself made herself fit to be received.
19.10: 19.10 And I fell, etc. Because I understood him greater than I, and was ready to obey, so do you also obey me. See thou do it not. In the old law he did not forbid himself to be adored; but after the ascension, seeing man exalted above himself, he feared to be adored by man. For the testimony, etc. Whatever the prophets said bears testimony to Christ.
19.11: 19.11 And I saw heaven opened. The damnation of Babylon told, and the exultation the saints will have thence, he adds the damnation of Antichrist himself and his apostles, which is there: And the beast was taken. And these, why will they be damned? because they fought against Christ as much as they could, and yet Christ will well be able to conquer, who has such power according to divinity and humanity that none can resist him, and therefore we ought to imitate him. Whence he himself interposes an admonition: And I saw one angel. I saw those called to the wedding, I saw also those who can come: for they have a good helper and good admonishers. A white horse, that is the flesh of Christ carrying the Word of God to battle against the devil.
19.12: 19.12 As a flame of fire. Because it burns vices, and kindles, and enlightens. All these things are said without respect to anyone, that we may note only what sort he is and how much he can do.
19.13: 19.13 The Word of God. That is: He spoke and they were made, Psalm 32.: through whom the Father made all things, and through whom the Father announced himself to the world.
19.14: 19.14 Clothed in fine linen, white and clean. That is, in clean bodies, who are restrained from unlawful things, and spurred by the goad of charity to good, that is to justice.
19.15: 19.15 A sharp two-edged sword. That is, the divine sentence, cutting wicked thoughts of the mind and unlawful motions of the body; or the Old and New Testament. He shall rule them. Advancing the saints from virtue to virtue, letting the wicked slip from vice to vice.
19.16: 19.16 And he has on his garment. Or in the hearts of the faithful who are the garment of the Son, is written: King of kings.
19.17: 19.17 And I saw one angel. The dignity of Christ having been shown, by which he will be able to overcome the devil, he adds an admonition for the present, as if he said: You ought to cleave to such a one. To all the birds. To all the faithful who are agile and light in promoting good works. Come, etc. By working well, in the same faith, not following diverse heresies like the wicked; or: from diverse parts of the world come to me. And gather yourselves. As if: You ought to be very careful that you may be able to come to this supper, because unless you fight well, you will succumb to the devil; because he is much prepared to harm you, yet with the help of God you will be able to overcome him.
19.20: 19.20 These two were cast alive. Namely Antichrist and his apostles will suffer greater punishments than others, in the likeness of one who is burned alive.
19.21: 19.21 And the rest were slain. That is, their followers will be punished with a lesser punishment, or those who shall be the rest, or converted to him, slain to the world, will live to God. And all the birds, that is all the saints, were filled with delight at their punishment, and at the progress of the brethren.
20.1: 20.1 And I saw an angel. The damnation of Babylon and of Antichrist and the false apostles told, he adds the damnation of the devil himself, and puts first the cause why and the time when he will be damned: and who can overcome him, namely he who in his humble coming could bind him as much as he willed, glorified will be able to destroy him altogether. Of the abyss. The dark abyss is what the hearts of the impious are called; or the devil himself, whom the Lord permits to rage and restrains when he wills.
20.2: 20.2 He laid hold. That is, he showed that devil to have sinned, while he killed one free from sin. He bound him. It is to be known that in like manner in Abraham and the other faithful the devil was bound as in these present; but in those the hope of the future Christ bound him, in these Christ himself coming bound him.
20.3: 20.3 And he cast him, etc. Because cast out from the faithful, he began to rule more atrociously among the wicked: so it is read in the Gospel that he entered into the swine. He sealed over him, etc. That is, he put a seal, namely the sign of the cross, which so overcomes him as to repel him from the faithful. And after these things he must, etc., that he receive the power he had before the coming of Christ.
20.4: 20.4 And I saw seats. The devil bound, I saw the faithful loosed, and the lesser ready to obey their prelates, and prelates to judge their subjects. I saw in the time of the binding the Church so loosed for well-doing, and in this same time, I saw those who die for Christ immediately enter into glory, never descend to hell, as Abraham and the other prophets descended, though they were just. And the souls of them that were beheaded. And I saw likewise the souls of those who did not adore. And they lived. And I do not say they will live and reign in the future, but even in this present, namely from the time they were slain they lived and reigned with Christ.
20.5: 20.5 But the rest of the dead did not live, that is they will suffer eternal punishments, and in this present, because they die at once. This is the resurrection. That the devil is so bound, and that men rise from sins, and that, they being dead, souls at once enjoy eternal rest, is the first resurrection and the chief. The first. To distinguish from that which will be at once in soul and body, this is called the first. He that has part. If all cannot be perfect, neither will they be in the same brightness. The second death, that is eternal damnation, which will be in the body and soul of the reprobate, shall not seize the elect, who are never increased in anything. But they shall be priests, that is offering eternal praises to the Divinity and humanity.
20.7: 20.7 Out of his prison. That is out of the hearts of the reprobate, in which he is now bound, that he not rage as he wills. Magog. That is uncovered, that is all persecutors covering the devil in themselves, and at length advancing to open persecution. Or literally he will first seduce these two nations, and through them proceed to others. And they compassed the camp of the saints, that is the same saints fortified in virtues and of one mind in this war.
20.10: 20.10 Day and night. He says this, in respect of the glory of the saints, which is day, and of their punishments, which is night.
20.11: 20.11 And I saw a throne. The destruction of the devil and his members told, he adds the destruction of the world, for the greater punishment of the impious. For it is fitting that when the wicked are destroyed the world be destroyed, according as it had been corrupted by them. Often having spoken of the glorification of the saints and the punishments of the impious, he had not made mention of the bodies, whether they were to be glorified or punished; therefore here he openly shows them.
20.12: 20.12 And the books were opened. Books, that is, the divine precepts, which those who left will know they are punished deservedly; or the books are the consciences of each, which will be open to all. Another book. That is Christ, who will then appear to all powerful and will give life to his own. Or, the book is the foreknowledge of God, because then the wicked will openly know they are not predestined to the life they promised themselves while in the world. Of those things which were written. By comparison with the saints the impious will be condemned: for the impious will read in those very saints what they would not do.
20.13: 20.13 And the sea gave up its dead. He wishes to show plainly that the bodies of the dead, however much dissolved, will be quickened in that judgment, which some do not believe.
20.14: 20.14 This is the second death. As if to say: Beware of the first death, because from that first follows this second.
21.1: 21.1 And I saw. In this seventh vision he treats of the renewal of the elements, the glorification of the saints, describing the merits by which the saints are so glorified. A new heaven and a new earth. The change of the air and earth, there is no doubt, will be by fire. But of the water there is doubt, for it is believed to have cleansing in itself.
21.2: 21.2 As a bride adorned. As the bridegroom sends gifts ahead to the bride before he leads her, so Christ gives the Church faith and virtues and good works before he receives her into glory.
21.3: 21.3 A great voice from the throne. When he had said he saw the renewal of the elements and the glorification of the saints, it was unknown, and, lest it seem incredible, he adds the authority of the holy Fathers, who foretold this. Behold the tabernacle. That is it is evident that in the same glory will be the humanity of Christ in which he fought, and men who imitated him and used these things well. And they shall be his people. That is, offending in nothing, which cannot be while they are in mortal flesh.
21.4: 21.4 And death. Truly there will be no tears there, because there will be no cause of tears.
21.5: 21.5 And he said. As if to say: Write whatever has been shown you of this renewal. This was done for the profit of those present, for whom I was commanded to write these things. Write: for these, etc. Commanding to write, and to announce to others, he adds an exhortation, that all may labor to belong to this renewal.
21.6: 21.6 And he said to me. The authority of the saints concerning this renewal having been put, he puts the authority of God himself. It is done. Lest anyone ask: What will be after that renewal, he is told nothing remains to be done. Alpha and Omega. As if to say: I shall be able to make this renewal, because I created all things, and in me all things shall be consummated. To him that thirsts. I will not give to him that thirsts for an hour, but to him that perseveres.
21.7: 21.7 He that shall overcome shall possess these things. That is, myself, who am the beginning of all beatitude.
21.8: 21.8 But the fearful. That is: to those who for fear of punishments flee from receiving the faith, or abandon it when received, will be eternal damnation.
21.9: 21.9 Come and I will show. The glory which the saints are to have having been described, he says by what merit, or by what help they will receive it.
21.10: 21.10 To a great mountain. Christ is the mountain, because the defense of his own is great, because he fills the whole world, high, because insuperable. He showed me the city. And upon that mountain he shows the foundation of the Church.
21.11: 21.11 Light. The heavenly Jerusalem herself shining according to her measure, is like Christ, who was firm in purpose, and shining in virtues. Of jasper. This stone is hard and green: so the Church shines with faith, and is made firm in it.
21.12: 21.12 A wall. That is Christ the defender, who is great in Sion, high with the Father. Or understand the defenders of others, who are great in overcoming others. Others lest they be overcome, that is the apostles or prophets, or angels messengers of truth. Twelve gates. That is the patriarchs, by whose example others are brought into the faith. Or the gates, the apostles, who bring others into the Church. Angels, that is subjects who, perfectly instructed, are put in the place of angels. The number of the gates, twelve, which through the four parts of the world are comprehended under a ternary, pertains to the mystery of the twelve apostles, through whom the faith of the Trinity is spread through the fourfold world. Names written, etc. That is the memory of the holy Fathers of the old law is in the apostles, because what those foretold would be, these teach as fulfilled. Or all nations are placed in the faith of the apostles and their love. Whence: You are our epistle written in our hearts, 2 Corinthians 3.
21.13: 21.13 On the east three gates. The east, the Jews: from whom the sun of justice rose, and in these three gates, because in these first the faith of the Trinity was announced by apostles and prophets. The north, the cold Gentiles: who believed after the Jews. From the south, that is from the brightness of faith, which is from the coming of Christ. From the west, that is from the last age of the world which through Elijah and Enoch will receive the faith of the Trinity.
21.14: 21.14 The wall. That is the faith of Christ by which he fortified the city itself, has twelve patriarchs, by whom it is founded, because those first held this faith, and on them whoever come to the faith lean. And in them twelve. Which faith these hold, those understood as to come, and foretold.
21.15: 21.15 And he that spoke with me. I saw that city so fortified and adorned, and I saw not all there equal among themselves: but each perfect in his own measure. A measure of a golden reed. That is, the divine Scripture composed by the wisdom of God, which touches and illumines the hearts of the faithful. That he might measure the city and the gates thereof. That is, according to measure he would give even to the lesser understanding of the Scriptures themselves. Is laid out four-square. The four sides, faith, hope, charity, working, which are equal, because as much as one believes, so much he hopes: as much as he hopes, so much he loves: as much as he loves, so much he works. In a square therefore, because robust in faith, long-suffering in hope, ample in charity, effective in work. Or the four sides are the four principal virtues, of which one ought not to exceed another. In man therefore is prudence of seeking good and avoiding evil, which temperance follows, that man withdraw from pleasures: after these fortitude, that he do what he understands: then justice, that he so temper his acts as not to seem to himself too just or wise. By furlongs. A furlong is a place and course and measure, and eight make a mile, and it notes those pressing on to the prize. Twelve thousand. These are perfect in the faith of the Trinity from the four parts of the world.
21.17: 21.17 The measure of a man. According to the letter Saint John shows that the angel appeared to him in the shape of a man, to denote plainly that he who was signified was the true angel, that is the Son of God, and true man.
21.18: 21.18 And it was. He had said in this city there are walls and gates and foundations, and these among themselves, some greater, some lesser, here he follows up what the wall is like and what the city itself and the foundations and gates. The structure of the wall of jasper stone. That is, if anyone be instructed for this, to be a defender of others, he has it from the faith which he firmly holds and preaches, which the green jasper signifies, to be a defender of others. Gold. Gold denotes wisdom; glass the purity of faith, by which he promises with the mouth what he believes with the heart.
21.19: 21.19 Jasper. This stone is green, and therefore signifies the unfading greenness of faith. Or the jasper is the faith of the saints, not withering, but ever persevering in the greenness of works. Sapphire. It is like a clear sky, which struck by the rays of the sun sends forth a burning brightness; it signifies the height of the hope of the saints whose conversation is in heaven, who also renewed by the true sun seek eternal things more ardently, and teach others to seek, saying: Our conversation is in heaven, Philippians 3. Chalcedony, BEDE. This stone has the color of a pale lamp: it shines, etc., down to sinners and the frail they draw to themselves and join to them. Emerald. THE SAME. The fourth of excessive greenness above all herbs and leaves, so that even, etc., down to the fourth is called faith on account of the four Gospels.
21.20: 21.20 Sardonyx. THE SAME. The fifth three-colored, black at the bottom, white, etc., down to what is done by the five senses, is called the fifth. Sardius. The sixth of one blood-red color signifies the glory of martyrdom. Sixth because on the sixth day Christ was crucified. Or the sardius having the look of red earth, signifies the saints who though exalted in understanding of mind, yet remember their frailty, considering themselves sons of Adam, who is called red earth, who was made on the sixth day, whence also the sardius is brought in as sixth. Beryl. BEDE. The eighth is the working of preachers. The beryl shines, etc., down to returning from the care of earthly administration to the paleness of the active life. Topaz. The ninth is put here, because this stone is rarer and more precious, and has two colors from gold and ethereal brightness, shining most when touched with the splendor of the sun, surpassing the brightness of all gems, singularly provoking beholders to its sight, which if you polish more, you obscure: if you leave to nature, it is brighter: and nothing is dearer to kings among riches. It signifies the contemplative life, which holy kings prefer to all riches of works and gems of virtues and direct their gaze to it above all, and so much the more, the more frequently they are illumined by divine grace. From inward charity the golden color, from the sweetness of contemplation the ethereal, which from the friction of the world always grows dim, for scarcely can anyone be touched with sorrows and at the same time look with tranquil mind on the joys of heaven. Or if you polish, that if you honor them with the dignities of the world, and adorn them, you obscure: because they have less leisure for contemplation, or become less in merits. And as in the eighth is the active life, so in the ninth the contemplative which is that of the angels, of whom there are nine orders. Some say that it has the colors of all stones, whence it has its name, because pan, that is all. And it is found in an island of Egypt, called Topazon, it signifies the saints shining with all the colors of virtues. Chrysoprase. In India is born green and golden mixture. Some also purple with golden drops, it signifies those who merit the greenness of the eternal country by charity, and show another purple of martyrdom, and because they follow the example of the Lord, they are in India, that is near the sunrise, and await to reign with Christ. They are in the tenfold number, the decalogue is fulfilled by love, which does not end. In the chrysoprase therefore the work of martyrdom and its reward is signified. Chryson, gold: prasos, leek is called. Hyacinth. The eleventh is this stone, changing with the air, clear in fair weather, dim in cloud, it signifies the most discreet teachers adapting themselves to all qualities, manners, ages, understandings. Amethyst. The twelfth stone is purple, with mixed color of violet and rose pouring forth certain little flames. The purple color signifies the habit of the heavenly kingdom, the principality of angelic society to which the saints are to come. The violet the humble modesty of the saints with the odor of good working. The rose the precious death of the martyrs, who not only among themselves but also toward enemies and persecutors send forth flames of charity. The amethyst therefore signifies the memory always of the heavenly kingdom in the hearts of the humble, and that excellent virtue, that they pray even for enemies, and care for their salvation, which is the virtue of virtues. The variety of colors the multiplicity of virtues.
21.21: 21.21 And the twelve gates. As if to say: I said there are twelve gates, and since those twelve gates are so, that is the prophets introducing to the faith of the Trinity from the four parts of the world. Each by itself, that is by the instruction of each; are pearls, that is the imitators of them, who from whatever part of the world are called to the faith of the Trinity, are splendid in virtues. Each gate, etc. As if to say: That they might be gates, they had to be pearls. The street of the city gold. That is wisdom, or full of brightness, clean from criminal stain. Glass transparent. That is hiding no filth in themselves. Or because the wicked can in their works, as in a mirror, recognize their wickedness.
21.23: 21.23 Has no need of the sun. Here the saints need sun and moon for service, there not: for God will fully illumine them. Or, has no need of sun nor moon, that is of greater or lesser preachers.
21.24: 21.24 And shall walk. So great will be the light in the future, that until the end of the world, the nations will walk, that is will be advanced from good to better. In the light. In hope of this light, or by the light, or by the light, or by the rays of the knowledge of it. The kings of the earth. That is those greater ones who rule their own earthliness and that of others.
21.25: 21.25 And the gates. In the present sometimes preaching is withdrawn, lest thieves enter and trample while it is night, that is the place of ambushes: but because there is perpetual day, all fear will be removed.
21.26: 21.26 They shall bring. In likeness of conquerors who carry spoils into their cities.
21.27: 21.27 There shall not enter into it. The honesty of the city told, lest any false brother presume to reach any of these degrees, he determines who are to enter, who not.
22.1: 22.1 And he showed. After he showed the site of the city, its dignity, and the walls and foundations, he describes the refreshment which God provided for the city, both in the present and chiefly in the future. In the presence of the Deity or imitation of the life of the Lamb, who set before us in himself an example. A river. That is flowing water, that is eternal beatitude. In the form of water is noted the ablution of baptism, by which one comes to this beatitude. From the seat of God. That is from those in whom God will chiefly sit, because he is in them most, and through their instruction the lesser will be crowned.
22.2: 22.2 And on both sides. Around the river, that is, in this life we have the tree of life, that is the body and blood of Christ, by which we are refreshed beyond the river, that is in the future we shall have him present. Or by around the river, we may take the time before baptism, by beyond, that which was after baptism, that we may denote the faithful saved through Christ both in the old and new law, which Moses signified who led the children of Israel to the river Jordan, and Joshua the son of Nun, who from the river Jordan led them into the promised land. The tree of life. As if to say: He himself gives refreshment, he also gives to them those who prepare those to whom he himself will render. Fruits. That is the prophets and apostles fruitful in the faith of the Trinity through the four parts of the world. And the leaves of the tree. As if to say: And that Christ will render fruit, this will be so, that the apostles, and after them others also, will scatter the leaves of Christ himself.
22.6: 22.6 And he said to me. As in the beginning he set the commendation of the vision, so also now at the last he sets it. The Lord. And well you ought to believe, because he who has in his power the gifts of the Holy Spirit, through whom all the prophets spoke what they said. His angel, etc. As the angel to John, so John commends to his disciples: as if to say: Not for my sake was this announcement made to me, but that you may believe me.
22.8: 22.8 And after I had heard and seen. Here he gives us to understand that for these things we ought to hold him in veneration, and not only him, but adore God, and by observing the words of the book obtain the purification of the angels.
22.9: 22.9 And of your brethren, etc. Those who have the grace of interpreting are not to be thought alien from the office of prophecy: such as Augustine, Jerome, Ambrose, Gregory, etc.
22.11: 22.11 He that hurts, let him hurt still. Because it could be objected that it would be evil to prophesy to the wicked, since they would be punished the more gravely for it, he is told not to cease on that account, because it is just.
22.14: 22.14 Blessed are they that wash, etc. Because he had said: Let the hurtful hurt, the filthy be filthy still, lest some wicked man say: Since I am wicked, why should I repent? he says. Not only are they blessed who reject the greater persecution, but also those who have defiled their robes received in baptism, if they afterward wash them, and repent of having sinned.
22.16: 22.16 I Jesus. John commended the book by the angel, by his own dignity, now also by the authority of Christ himself. As if to say: Let all who hear know that I Jesus have sent my angel to testify to you these things. The bright star. A clear star, that is great charity announcing the day, that is the future beatitude, made in the morning through my resurrection.
22.17: 22.17 And the spirit, that is the Trinity, which for the excellence of purity is called spirit: And the spirit and the bride say, etc. Here also he adds the testimony of the Trinity and of the faithful, as if: Therefore you ought to receive it, because the spirit and the bride, etc. And let him that thirsts come. Not any one, however, but let him only come who thirsts: that is desires to believe. And he that will, let him take the water of life freely. And there is no labor, because the will alone suffices.
22.18: 22.18 For I testify, etc. After he had set the commendation through himself, through the angel, through Christ, through the Trinity, through the faithful; since he knew there were some in Asia who to foster their errors would add or take away something, he adds an excommunication.
22.21: 22.21 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. The consummation of the apostle in the word of Christ.
